finding: The strict closed-cone strengthening of the mixed-band direct selector can be reduced exactly to a one-dimensional intersection of at most 54,912 affine theta inequalities. The fixed-odd stable-even-box cone is full-dimensional and pointed in eight dimensions with 14 defining inequalities; enumerate its extreme rays by the at-most C(14,7)=3432 signed cofactor null vectors, retain feasible orientations, and evaluate the 16 direct odd-ray/endpoint functionals on each. Their positivity bounds give exact rational or real-algebraic lower and upper envelopes. A solution is sufficient for a uniform direct five-node exclusion. A zero at a boundary ray does not disprove the open-cone selector; the Motzkin LP remains the exact open-cone criterion. A strict crossing U<L with (U,L) intersecting (0,1) yields two explicit rationalizable full-width stable boxes that rule out the uniform selector, but not an original no-go. No universal envelope inequality or actual crossing is claimed.
